newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ says Q1 performance as expected.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ says Q1 performance as expected.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) said on Wednesday that its financial performance in the first quarter to end-December was very much as expected, with falling interest margins.
"However, this is being offset by continued growth in lending assets and increased fee income," ANZ chairman Charles Goode told the annual general meeting.

He said core costs, which excluded retrenchment costs and direct revenue costs, were stable at the level of the second half of 1996. "We see no sign of deterioration in our asset quality, which remains very good," Goode said.
Goode said that as anticipated, cuts in mortgage lending rates had led to a fall in interest margins.

"In the current financial year, we see in Australia a continuation of the present subdued business conditions for the next six months with the prospect of an acceleration in economic activity later in 1997," he said.

Goode said ANZ expected to see tangible evidence of the benefits of the restructuring of its domestic banking businesses in Australia and New Zealand. "We also expect to see higher profits flowing from the development of our international banking operations," he said.

"There is significant potential growth to come from the globalisation of our investment banking and cards businesses and we will also be actively looking for opportunities to expand our funds management operations," Goode said.

ANZ reported a net profit of A$1.12 billion for the year to September 30, up from A$1.05 billion in the previous year, but said when it released its results in November that it expected margins to contract further in the year ahead.
Goode said ANZ's priority in Australia and New Zealand was to restructure its businesses to meet the challenges created by intense competition. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
